A control you can show and a control you can only describe are treated as two different things. This review produces that evidence, obligation by obligation, and marks each one held, partial or absent.

Request an Assurance Review

What this is

Assurance Review

An Assurance Review is an independent assessment of the controls governing your organization's AI systems. It tests them against ISO/IEC 42001, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and the local requirements that apply. It produces an evidence ledger showing which obligations are supported by artifacts that exist, which are partially supported, and which are not supported at all.

Questions We Are Asked

Is this an ISO 42001 certification?
It prepares you for certification. The review assesses your controls against ISO/IEC 42001 and assembles the evidence a certification body will ask for, so the certification audit starts from a tested position. The certificate itself is issued by an accredited certification body, which keeps that opinion independent.
What is an evidence ledger?
A matrix of the obligations an organization is subject to against the artifacts that would satisfy them (policy, inventory, risk assessment, evaluation result, decision record, monitoring output). Each cell is marked held, partial or absent. It replaces a maturity score, which can be argued with, with a statement of what is missing.
Do we need an AI inventory first?
In practice, yes. The assessment samples against the inventory, so an absent or partial inventory limits what can be concluded. Organizations without one usually run an AI Estate Inventory first, or accept a narrower scope covering a named subset of systems.
Can you assure systems you built for us?
Yes, with an independent opinion. Orvix builds and operates systems, and it assesses them. Where an assurance opinion is needed on a system we built or operate, it is written by a party that does not report to the delivery team, or by a fully independent third party when it needs external weight. That separation is what gives the opinion its value.
Who is the deliverable written for?
Three audiences, in one package. A ledger and roadmap for the team closing the gaps, a summary a board or risk committee can adopt as a position, and an evidence pack assembled so it can be produced to an examiner or a customer without being rebuilt.
